newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Funeral of Ethiopian crown prince set for Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Funeral of Ethiopian crown prince set for Sunday.

text.p: The funeral of Ethiopia's crown prince, who named himself emperor in exile, will be held in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa on Sunday, family members said.

They said the body of 80-year-old Crown Prince Asfaw Wossen Haile Selassie would arrive in Addis Ababa aboard a plane from the United States on Saturday night and the funeral would take place at the Ethiopian Orthodox Trinity Cathedral on Sunday.
Other details of the death were not immediately available.
He will buried following a requiem mass in a royal tomb prepared during the rule of his father Emperor Haile Selassie, who ruled for 40 years and was killed in detention in 1975 at the age of 83.
Asfaw Wossen's wife Princess Medferiash-work Abebe, his son Zera-Yacob, other members of the exiled royal family, former aristocrats and royalists were expected to attend the funeral.
The government views the crown prince's funeral simply as that of an individual and no officials are expected to attend.
Asfaw Wossen crowned himself in exile in 1988 as Amha Selassie -- Ethiopia's 226th emperor in the line of the King of Kings said to extend 3,000 years to King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.
He died after a long illness. Despite being crippled by a stroke, he had said he wanted to return to Ethiopia as a constitutional monarch after rebels overthrew its Marxist rulers in 1991.
Asfaw Wossen was evacuated to London in 1973, a year after the military ousted Haile Selassie, for medical treatment.

The remains of Haile Selassie, exhumed from under a toilet in the grounds of the imperial palace in 1990, rest in a royal mausoleum in Addis Ababa with other former rulers including Emperor Menelike II.

A total of 46 former members of the military junta, the Dergue, are being tried in Addis Ababa on charges of genocide and other crimes including the murder of Haile Selassie, whose royal titles included Elect of God and the Lion of Judah.
